name: NInfer-4090 Extreme (Acelogic/ninfer-4090-extreme)
models_supported: VERIFIED: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GGUF (src/flashnext/), Qwen3.8-27B, Ternary Bonsai 2 27B; GGUF types F32/F16/BF16/Q8_0/Q6_K/IQ4_NL/IQ3_S/IQ4_XS only, no Q4_K/Q5_K (src/flashnext/gguf.h:17-26)
hardware: VERIFIED: CUDA sm_89 only (CMakeLists.txt:3-12); host ISA x86-64-v4 + AVX512-VNNI required for Flash-Next (src/flashnext/CMakeLists.txt:37-42); Windows 11 is the built and measured platform
offload_methods: VERIFIED: VRAM expert cache in a cuMemMap elastic arena + all routed experts in pinned RAM (lossless repack Q4L/Q4X/IQ4L/Q8_0), CPU computes misses or GPU reads them zero-copy; attention KV paged through pinned RAM above 32K (docs/maintainer/flash-next-engine.md §3.1, §3.9)
scheduler: VERIFIED: one CUDA graph per decode step (1-4 tokens); per layer GPU writes ids to a mapped ExpertLink and raises a flag, host thread spins, runs CpuExperts::run, raises a flag (engine.cpp:1721 host_experts); decode-time cache adaptation, 192 swaps/step max (engine.cpp:2335 AdaptParams)
kernels: VERIFIED: own CUDA GEMV/GEMM/QSA/expert kernels (src/flashnext/cuda/*.cu); CPU expert kernels AVX-512 only (src/flashnext/cpu_experts.cpp: 223 lines with _mm512), no AVX2 path
multi_gpu: VERIFIED: single GPU (one device_ in vram.cpp; no split code in src/flashnext)
long_context_262k: REPORTED: 262K window, needle at 250K retrieved, 45.1 tok/s plain / 44.9 MTP at 250K depth (flash-next-engine.md §4.5, 1x4090 + 7950X)
overlap_gpu_cpu_ssd: VERIFIED: GPU cached experts || CPU uncached experts in the same layer; background swaps on own stream; no SSD tier for experts (GGUF mmap for PLE)
benchmarks: REPORTED: 1x RTX 4090 + Ryzen 9 7950X DDR5 (55-62 GB/s), UD-IQ4_XS 94 GB: 50-60 tok/s short, ~44 at 256K, prefill 2,500-3,000 tok/s (README; flash-next-engine.md §2, §4.5)
independent_confirmation: NOT FOUND: single author's runs on one box
limitations: VERIFIED: AVX-512 host kernels (Zen 3 EPYC has AVX2 only); single GPU; no Q4_K/Q5_K experts so UD-Q4_K_XL does not load; UD-IQ4_XS has IQ3_S gate/up (<4 bit, research/README.md); Windows-first tooling
key_code: src/flashnext/engine.cpp:host_experts — per-layer CPU side of the GPU/CPU expert handshake
src/flashnext/engine.cpp:AdaptParams (Decode-time adaptation) — decayed-use expert swaps between steps
src/flashnext/cpu_experts.cpp:CpuExperts::run — AVX-512 VNNI expert GEMV over lossless repacks
src/flashnext/cuda/kv_stream.cu — attention KV paged from pinned RAM
portability_to_us: HYPOTHESIS: low as an engine (single GPU, AVX-512, no Q4_K); design reference for an sm_89 Qwen3.8-FN runtime (adaptation policy, KV paging, exact FP32 numerics)
adaptation_cost: HYPOTHESIS: AVX2 port of cpu_experts + Q4_K/Q5_K readers + multi-GPU split = months
testable_without_target_hw: HYPOTHESIS: partly: sm_89 compile in CI; CPU kernels need an AVX-512 box; adaptation policy replayable offline from NINFER_FN_ROUTING_DUMP traces
potential_impact: HYPOTHESIS: medium (ideas for Qwen3.8-FN, which fits our VRAM anyway)

name: SSD-LLaMA (arXiv 2609.18110)
sha: NOT FOUND (no code repository found; searches in R12-gapfill.md)
models_supported: REPORTED: DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Kimi-K2.7-Code, GLM-5.2, Kimi-K3 (paper summary)
hardware: REPORTED: RTX 5090 32 GB + 16-32 GB RAM + one PCIe 5.0 NVMe (9 GiB/s), Intel Ultra5 230F
offload_methods: REPORTED: SSD holds every expert; per-expert contiguous pack; RAM and VRAM caches (frequency + recency); io_uring direct parallel reads; optional rANS lossless compression decoded on GPU
scheduler: REPORTED: demand reads after the router (no predictive prefetch); CPU/GPU split chosen by measured token latency; on the 5090 the all-GPU split won
kernels: REPORTED: built on llama.cpp; CUDA rANS decoder
long_context_262k: REPORTED: short-context benchmarks only (MMLU/Alpaca); KV management out of scope
overlap_gpu_cpu_ssd: REPORTED: per-request H2D starts as each io_uring read completes
benchmarks: REPORTED: decode 2.10-15.58x and prefill 1.52-4.19x vs llama.cpp/KTransformers/Colibri; Kimi-K2.7-Code 1.03 tok/s with 32 GB RAM; Kimi-K3 0.465 tok/s
limitations: REPORTED: 1-2 tok/s class, SSD-bound; prefetch hides ~5% on GLM-5.2 per the authors; KV out of scope
portability_to_us: HYPOTHESIS: low: our GLM UD-Q4_K_XL experts fit VRAM+RAM, NVMe is not a per-token weight tier (R8 §3)
testable_without_target_hw: HYPOTHESIS: pack layout and io_uring read path testable on any Linux NVMe box
potential_impact: HYPOTHESIS: low for GLM/Qwen; only relevant if DeepSeek-V4.1 experts spill to NVMe

name: SGLang SSD Expert Pack (sgl-project/sglang)
models_supported: VERIFIED: expert packs for DeepSeek-V4(-Flash) and Kimi-K3 GGML (model_loader/expert_pack/prepare_deepseek_pack.py, prepare_kimi_pack.py); no GLM-5.3-Flash pack script
hardware: REPORTED: one RTX 5090 32 GB + Intel Ultra5 230F + 32 GB RAM + 2 TB PCIe 5.0 SSD (lmsys blog source, lm-sys.github.io blog/2026-08-29-sglang-ssd-expert-pack.md:17)
offload_methods: VERIFIED: SSD-resident 'SGLANG-EXPERTPACK-v1' file (gate/up/down per layer-expert contiguous), pinned staging slots, GPU slot cache sized in MiB (layers/moe/expert_pack.py:232 ExpertPackStore)
scheduler: VERIFIED: demand fetch per MoE layer: topk ids copied to host, misses read with os.preadv in 4 splits on a thread pool, H2D on a transfer stream, compute waits on events (expert_pack.py:507 acquire); no prediction, no CPU expert compute
kernels: VERIFIED: no new kernels; uses SGLang MoE kernels on the slot cache
overlap_gpu_cpu_ssd: VERIFIED: limited: reads of one layer's misses overlap each other, not the layer's compute (acquire blocks the current stream on the copies)
benchmarks: REPORTED (blog source :250-253, :280, :286): DeepSeek-V4-Flash decode 1.99/1.85 tok/s (Alpaca/MMLU, n=5 each) vs 0.29/0.28 baseline; unique-key VRAM hit 54%/46%; SSD 1.66-2.04 GB per generated token; Kimi-K3 hit 17-23%, 22-28 GB/token
limitations: VERIFIED: host sync per layer (topk_ids.cpu()); victim = lowest frequency among LRU, active top-k protected (expert_pack.py:464 _victim_slot); O_DIRECT optional (direct_io flag)
portability_to_us: HYPOTHESIS: low as a decode path (per-token NVMe weight reads, R8 §3); the identity-checked pack format is a good model for our own NVMe artefacts
adaptation_cost: HYPOTHESIS: n/a for GLM (SGLang GLM path blocked on sm_89, R7 §1.3)
testable_without_target_hw: HYPOTHESIS: pack build/validate logic on CPU; I/O path on any NVMe box
confidence: medium (code read at the SHA; numbers second-hand)

name: fomoe (pmerolla/fomoe) - cache-aware routing, 3-tier expert cache
models_supported: REPORTED: Qwen3.5-397B and -122B GGUF Q4_K_M (README, 397b.freq/122b.freq profiles)
hardware: VERIFIED: HIP/ROCm gfx1200 GPU build (Makefile, src/gpu_kernels.hip); CPU -march=native; REPORTED box 2x RX 9060 XT, 32 GB DDR5, Gen5 NVMe
offload_methods: VERIFIED: VRAM slots per layer (src/expert_cache.c vram_cache_*), pinned DRAM slots (ram_cache_*), full expert store on NVMe read with io_uring, one ring per drive (src/nvme_io.c drive_io_thread)
scheduler: VERIFIED: frequency-profile seeding (vram_cache_seed), prefetch classify/submit (src/prefetch.c), background backfill of substituted experts; 'ping-pong' layer alternation over 2 GPUs
kernels: VERIFIED: own HIP kernels (src/gpu_kernels.hip), C CPU expert path (src/cpu_expert.c)
multi_gpu: VERIFIED: 2 GPUs, even/odd layers, hidden state via pinned memory, no all-reduce (README; src/tp.hip)
overlap_gpu_cpu_ssd: REPORTED: NVMe backfill during attention, H2D from DRAM tier
benchmarks: REPORTED: Qwen3.5-397B Q4_K_M 5.1 tok/s exact, 8.8 tok/s with CAR 0.35 at +3.5% WikiText PPL (README)
limitations: VERIFIED: CAR substitutes a cached expert for an uncached one and renormalises (src/car.c:36 car_evaluate) = changes routing, lossy; AMD-only GPU code
key_code: src/car.c:car_evaluate — cache-aware routing (substitute if score ratio >= threshold)
portability_to_us: HYPOTHESIS: none for CAR (exact routing required); per-drive io_uring rings are a reference for an NVMe tier
testable_without_target_hw: HYPOTHESIS: CAR quality effect measurable on CPU with a small MoE
